parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 1-3
items: A calling that predates the called - known, sanctified, and appointed before being formed
The qualification for speaking is never eloquence but sending; the mouth is touched, not trained
Yahweh watching over His word to perform it - the almond branch as the guarantee of the boiling pot
A lawsuit that opens with a wedding memory and a question: what unrighteousness did you find in me?
Two evils, not one - forsaking the spring, and the exhausting labor of digging cisterns that leak
Denial as the deeper guilt: "I have not sinned" is what finally brings the verdict
Mercy that cites the law it is about to overrule, and calls home a wife with no legal standing to return
Acknowledgment as the only condition - the door opens the moment the truth is told
The symbol retired because the reality arrives - an ark not missed, a throne in its place

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 4-6
items: Repentance as labor, not sentiment - hard ground broken open before any seed goes in
The covenant sign moved from the flesh to the heart, where Deuteronomy always aimed it
Judgment as de-creation: the light withdrawn and the void returning, over the same waters where light was first spoken
A pardon offered for the sake of one righteous man, and a city that could not produce him
Prosperity as the occasion of betrayal - fed to the full, and unfaithful because of it
The sea held back by sand, obeying a decree that a reasoning people refuse
False peace as malpractice - a dressing laid over a wound nobody cleaned
The ancient paths still standing open, with rest for the soul promised to whoever will walk them
A refining fire that cannot produce silver when there is nothing precious left in the ore
"Yet will I not make a full end" - the remnant clause that keeps every threat from being final

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 7-9
items: A holy place treated as a charm - the address mistaken for the relationship
Shiloh as the standing proof that Yahweh's name on a site is no guarantee for the site
Worship measured at the gate: the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow as the actual test
Obedience commanded before sacrifice, at the exodus and ever since
Migratory birds keeping appointed times that a Torah-holding people no longer recognize
A season with a closing date - harvest past, summer ended, and the window shut
Balm available and physicians present, with the wound left untreated by choice
Speech as the engine of estrangement - tongues trained to lie until deceit becomes hard work
Grief so large it requires professional mourners and has to be taught to the next generation
Wisdom, might, and riches disqualified as boasts; knowing Yahweh left standing alone
Circumcision of the flesh without circumcision of the heart, counted with the nations

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 10-12
items: Gods that must be nailed upright and carried, set beside the God whose voice moves the weather
Idols as powerless in both directions - unable to harm, and equally unable to help
The living God, the true God, the everlasting King - three titles no manufactured thing can hold
Leadership that stopped inquiring, and a flock scattered as the direct result
The humblest prayer in the book: I cannot direct my own steps; correct me, but gently
A covenant read aloud with its curse intact, and a prophet who says Amen to terms that bind him too
Devotion counted by inventory - a god for every city, an altar for every street
The gentle lamb who did not know, and the hometown that wanted him silenced
A complaint filed inside the relationship: You are righteous, and I still want to argue
An answer that is training rather than explanation - footmen now, horses ahead
Yahweh's own grief named plainly: the dearly beloved of My soul, handed over
A door left open even for the nations who plundered, if they will learn to swear by His name

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 13-15
items: Covenant as clinging, not merely compliance - a people meant to be worn against Yahweh like linen
Pride as the specific rot that pries a nation loose, and separation that ruins without needing an enemy
Sin that becomes second nature, and the honest admission that no leopard changes its own spots
Drought, empty cisterns, and the physical world preaching what the pulpits refused to say
The lying comfort of unsent prophets, and the fact that being deceived is not the same as being innocent
Intercession forbidden - the terrible mercy of a door that a people themselves closed
Yahweh's own grief inside His judgment: tears commanded, not merely permitted
A prophet's raw complaint brought straight to God, accusation and all, and not edited out of Scripture
Words eaten as food, and the loneliness that comes with digesting them
Repentance asked of the messenger, and a bronze wall promised only on the far side of it

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 16-18
items: A prophet's own life conscripted as the sermon - obedience that costs marriage, mourning, and company
Judgment announced and restoration promised in the same breath, with a second exodus greater than the first
Two root systems, two futures - trust in flesh that withers, trust in Yahweh that stays green in drought
A heart no one can read except the One who made it, and who says plainly that He searches it
The Sabbath as the ordinary, concrete gate where covenant loyalty is either carried or set down
Sovereignty as a working hand rather than a fixed script - the marred vessel remade, not discarded
The offer of return standing open until a people themselves close it with "It is in vain"
The cost of carrying the word: conspiracy from priest, sage, and prophet, and lament brought honestly to Yahweh

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 19-21
items: Sign-acts that escalate: soft clay remade on the wheel, then fired clay broken beyond mending
A holiness that cannot even imagine what His people had normalized - "it didn't enter into my mind"
Places renamed by what happens in them, and a valley whose name became a word for judgment
The stiffened neck as the root cause, with every atrocity downstream of a refusal to hear
Violence against the messenger as the standard institutional response to an unwanted word
Fire in the bones - a call that cannot be resigned from even when obeying it costs everything
Faith and grief held in the same hour, praise and lament left side by side without resolution
Prayer requested too late, and the exodus arm turned around to fight the city it once delivered
A door still standing open inside a sealed verdict - life offered on terms that humble before they save
Judgment as harvest rather than arbitrary wrath: the fruit of our own doings handed back to us

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 22-24
items: Knowing Yahweh defined as doing justice - the poor and needy as the instrument that measures a heart
Power audited by how it treats the powerless, with unpaid wages weighed as heavily as idolatry
The Davidic promise held and threatened at once: kings plucked off like a signet, the line never ended
A stump felled and a Branch raised - Yahweh growing something out of what He Himself cut down
Yahweh Our Righteousness: a King who supplies righteousness rather than merely demanding it
Yahweh taking up the shepherd's work Himself when every appointed shepherd has scattered the flock
The test of a true word - not eloquence or accuracy, but whether the speaker has stood in His council
A God who fills heaven and earth against a God kept conveniently local and manageable
Circumstances read wrongly: exile as mercy, an intact life as judgment, and the baskets reversed
A heart to know Him given as a gift, with wholehearted return as the fruit of the gift and not its price

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 25-27
items: A God who rises up early to send prophets, and twenty-three years of preaching met with silence
Judgment given a boundary - seventy years, an end date set by the One who set the discipline
Sovereignty grounded in creation: the earth given to whom He chooses, including to kings who never asked
The cup of wrath poured out on every nation, beginning at the city that carries His name
The word delivered whole - "don't omit a word" - and the temptation to soften named in advance
Shiloh as the standing proof that a sanctuary is not a guarantee
Faithfulness without a guarantee of survival: Jeremiah spared, Uriah extradited and killed
Providence with a name and an address - one official whose hand kept a prophet alive
Submission commanded as the way to live, and never presented as permanent
Prophetic office measured by intercession rather than prediction, and the homecoming that ends every hard word

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 28-30
items: False comfort that looks identical to the real thing - same venue, same formula, same God invoked
Fulfillment as the only test of a peace-prophecy, and the discipline of waiting for it
Resistance that hardens discipline rather than removing it: wooden bars replaced with iron
Trust as the thing at stake - the charge is not error but making a people trust in a lie
Ordinary faithfulness in exile: build, plant, marry, multiply, and pray for the city that took you
A promise of a future spoken to people who would not live to see it, and sturdier for that
Grace upstream of return - He is found by those who seek with the whole heart, and He promises to be found
Circumstances misread again: the deported were the good figs, the ones left behind were not
Pain not skipped on the way to comfort - labor pains, and a trouble named and bounded in one breath
"Therefore" as the hinge of the gospel: the wound's incurability is the reason He heals it

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 31-33
items: Love that precedes the drawing - everlasting first, and the turning as its consequence
Repentance asked for as a gift: "Turn me, and I will be turned"
A God whose insides churn over His people, described in the language of a parent rather than a judge
Inherited fate retired - each person answering for his own iniquity, and the sour-grapes excuse withdrawn
A new covenant whose newness is location rather than content: the same Torah, moved from stone to heart
Sin forgiven and deliberately not remembered, as the ground of the whole arrangement
Obedience before understanding - a field bought at full price in a city about to fall
Honest prayer that begins in confidence and ends in confusion, and is answered rather than rebuked
God's own question handed back to us: is there anything too hard for me?
Promises anchored to sunrise and sea, so that the covenant fails only if creation does
The demolition list read backward - silenced joy restored, an incurable wound healed, Hinnom made holy

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 34-36
items: Repentance anchored to fear rather than to God, and how quickly it reverses when pressure lifts
Liberty as a covenant obligation, and the terrible symmetry of a liberty proclaimed back to us
Oaths sworn in His house that drag His name into our reversals
Covenant as self-curse - walking between the pieces and meaning it
A word's weight measured by the standing of the one who spoke it
Outsiders who obeyed a dead ancestor for two centuries, against a nation that would not hear the living God
Faithfulness distinguished from rigidity: the Rechabites moved into the city and were still commended
The same words meeting three audiences and exposing three hearts in a single day
Josiah's torn robe against Jehoiakim's penknife - the family resemblance that failed to carry
Providence with no visible machinery: "but Yahweh hid them"
A word that cannot be destroyed, and opposition that only makes it longer

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 37-39
items: The danger of good news read wrongly - a reprieve mistaken for a rescue
Self-deception named as the real enemy: "do not lift up your own souls"
Curiosity about God's word that never becomes obedience to it
A king with all the authority who will not use it, overruled by men he outranks
The fear of being mocked as a sufficient cause for national catastrophe
An outsider with no standing doing the one right thing nobody else would do
Compassion measured in details - rags under the armpits before the ropes pull
Truth spoken unchanged to the man who controls whether you eat
Providence working through foreign hands: protection from the empire, not from the covenant people
God keeping a different ledger - a nation in rubble, a servant named and preserved
Trust as the stated reason for deliverance, in a man outside the covenant community

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 40-42
items: Freedom offered and comfort declined - a prophet choosing rubble over imperial patronage
Accurate theology from an unexpected mouth, and the shame of an outsider saying it better
The brief, real restoration that ordinary obedience produced at Mizpah
Goodness without discernment: a credible warning treated as slander, and a remnant scattered for it
Hospitality violated, grief counterfeited, and infrastructure built for life turned to a grave
Fear of consequences never verified, driving a people toward the one place they were forbidden
A model prayer for guidance offered by people who had already decided
Ten days of silence as part of the answer, and what waiting exposes in us
A God who says He grieves over the distress He Himself brought
Mercy promised inside an enemy's heart, and safety located in the frightening option
Self-deception named for what it is - dealing deceitfully against our own souls

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 43-45
items: Denying the commission when the message cannot be answered - "Yahweh has not sent you"
Blaming the scribe: how a word gets dismissed by finding someone to blame for it
Fear rewriting a promise into a threat, and then arguing with its own version
A homecoming undone by the people who survived to enjoy it
God still speaking on the wrong side of a border - disobedience changes the address, not the relationship
Prophecy done with the hands: stones in wet mortar at a foreign king's door
Empires as instruments - "Nebuchadnezzar my servant" - and the gods of Egypt worn like a coat
Idolatry as self-harm: great evil committed against our own souls
Correlation mistaken for covenant, and a nation's worship ordered around the years that went well
The domestic idol, taught in kitchens and passed down, harder to remove than any state religion
Being handed over to what we insisted on - "perform your vows" as a sentence, not a permission
A name withdrawn from the mouth that used it as a formality
The one question underneath the whole book: whose word will stand, mine or theirs
A tired servant heard by name, his complaint quoted back without mockery
Ambition set down for a season, and life itself received as spoil

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 46-48
items: A defeated kingdom's prophet announcing the fate of empires - jurisdiction claimed over the whole map
Nations armed, mustered, and paid for, collapsing anyway because Yahweh pushed them
Imperial ambition described in the language of the thing the empire worshipped
Hired strength that goes home, and a Pharaoh who is only a noise
"Terror on every side" - the prophet's own taunt turned outward
A full end for the nations, no full end for Jacob, and correction that comes in measure
A sword under orders, and the human plea to sheathe it that Scripture keeps and does not answer
Fathers who cannot turn back for their children, recorded without comment
Comfort as a spiritual danger - wine that was never poured from vessel to vessel
Trust placed in works, treasures, and a god who ends up on a cart
Pride stacked four words deep, and mockery of a fallen brother named as the offense
Boasting that God simply calls nothing
A God who wails for the nation He is breaking, with funeral pipes sounding in His own heart
Latter-day clauses granted to Egypt and Moab - the door left open for outsiders
A Moabite great-grandmother in the line of David, standing behind the mercy in verse 47

parts.title: Major Themes Across Jeremiah 49-52
items: Yahweh's jurisdiction running to the edge of the map, and a throne set in Elam
Doors left open in the latter days - Moab, Ammon, Elam, Egypt - and no explanation given for who gets one
Provision promised to enemy orphans and widows in the middle of a judgment speech
Pride at altitude: nests built high in the rock, and hearts deceived by the view
Submit to Babylon, and know Babylon is finished - two truths held at once for forty years
The instrument that is not therefore innocent, and a crime that was the enjoyment of the work
A search made for the sin of a people, and nothing found
A strong Redeemer, go'el, standing up in court for relatives who cannot pay
The hammer of the whole earth broken after the work is done
A golden cup in God's own hand, and healing attempted before judgment fell
Creation set against the idols - the same sermon preached to Judah and then to Babylon
A word delivered to its address, read aloud to nobody, and sunk in a river
Grief that counts pomegranates, and a nation reduced to a four-digit ledger entry
Everything warned about, happening exactly, down to the day
And a son of David out of prison, in clean clothes, given bread every day until he died
